quarterly_data.quarter: Taiyo Yuden press release: Summary of Q&A for the Earnings Release Conference for the (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Q1 Q&A summary): sales of capacitors for AI servers grew around 80% YoY in Q1, in line with the initial forecast; demand is stronger than expected and the company now anticipates full-year growth of 150% YoY (May expectation: 80%). Server applications were 6% or more of total company sales last fiscal year and are expected to exceed the 10% level this fiscal year.
quarterly_data.figure: AI-server capacitor sales: Q1 around +80% YoY; FY forecast now +150% YoY; servers >10% of sales

quarterly_data.quarter: Taiyo Yuden press release: Summary of Q&A for the Earnings Release Conference for the (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management: capacitor capacity utilization expected around 95% in Q2, with a similarly high level continuing in the second half; no yield issues on AI server products. Under the Medium-term Management Plan 2030 capacitor capacity expansion is planned at about 10% annually, but next fiscal year the company plans to expand capacity by approximately 10%-15% YoY to meet stronger-than-expected AI server demand.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 capacitor utilization around 95%; capacity +10%-15% YoY next fiscal year

quarterly_data.quarter: Taiyo Yuden press release: Summary of Q&A for the Earnings Release Conference for the (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management outlook: from Q2 the operating margin is expected to exceed 10% on AI server sales growth and higher utilization; net sales expected to peak in Q3 with a more moderate than usual seasonal Q4 decline, so second-half operating profit above the first half. Fixed costs expected to rise 3.5 billion yen in Q2. Of the 40.0 billion yen net sales forecast increase, around 20.0 billion yen is currency and around 6.0 billion yen selling prices.
quarterly_data.figure: OPM >10% from Q2; revision includes ~20.0 billion yen FX and ~6.0 billion yen price

quarterly_data.quarter: Taiyo Yuden press release: Summary of Q&A for the Earnings Release Conference for the (08-19-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management on pricing and allocation: price revisions so far cover a limited proportion of products, mainly items with clearly excessive distributor orders; the supply and demand environment is showing signs of overheating and no decision on further revisions has been made. With limited capacity the policy is to increase supply primarily to automotive and IT infrastructure/industrial equipment including AI servers, serving existing customers elsewhere rather than gaining further share in smartphones or PCs. Q1 disruptions: Middle East-related shipping congestion in Malaysia and Singapore delayed parts and materials, affecting the Malaysia production site for about a week; a labor dispute at the South Korean site reduced operations for just under a month and was resolved in April.
